sources.entry: SwitchShuttle - Simple commands shortcut menu for macOS.

summary.one_liner: SwitchShuttle is a cross-platform system tray app (Rust, Tauri, Vue.js) for organizing and running terminal commands via menus, global hotkeys, and a CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define terminal commands in JSON configuration files or a visual editor, then run them from the system tray menu, with global hotkeys, or from the command line (by ID or name, with list and search). Commands can be organized in nested submenus, take dynamic inputs, and run in your chosen terminal (iTerm, Terminal, Warp, Alacritty, Hyper) in the current window, a new tab, or a new window. Background commands run as app-managed jobs shown under Running in the tray, with a Stop option. Switch commands show on/off state for toggles, monitor commands display live output in the menu, and scheduled commands run on six-field cron expressions. A security manager validates commands against length limits, blocked lists, and regex patterns before saving.
use_cases: Launch frequently used development commands from the menu bar or tray
Toggle system settings like WiFi, Bluetooth, or dark mode with one click
Run scheduled backups or recurring tasks with cron expressions
Monitor CPU, memory, disk, or network output from the tray
Run terminal commands from scripts or the command line by name
Organize team or personal shell snippets into nested menus
notable: Global hotkeys and nested submenus for launching shell commands from anywhere
Switch commands that toggle system features and show their current state
Monitor commands that show live system resource output in the tray menu
Command-line interface to run commands by ID, name, or search
caveats: Terminal options vary by OS: iTerm, Warp, and Terminal support differ across macOS, Windows, and Linux
Processes started in Terminal.app or iTerm cannot be stopped from the tray
Building from source requires Rust, Node.js 16+, pnpm, and Tauri CLI; Linux needs several GTK/WebKit system packages
